expectations.evidence: Amended tickets.md (TKT-014..TKT-016, a prose contract in the header, '## Not in scope for overdue tickets', '## Open questions') and cli.md (CLI-010..CLI-012; CLI-001 and CLI-006 amended; '## Open questions'). expectations.text: The spec has a one-paragraph intro, a `Prefix:` line, and a Non-goals section with at least two non-goals that are real boundaries (for example no notifications, no SLA pause on weekends, no change to the event log format).
expectations.evidence: Intro paragraph added to the tickets.md header: 'Overdue is a condition that the help desk derives from the current time, not a state...'. 'Prefix: `TKT`.' follows. '## Not in scope for overdue tickets' lists 5 boundaries (no new state or event kind, no due-time change or business hours, no alerts, no late-closure report, no lateness amount). The intro paragraph is an invariant statement rather than a feature description.

expectations.text: At least five criteria headed `### PREFIX-NNN: Title` with zero-padded three-digit numbers (a letter suffix such as TKT-014A is allowed), unique within the file; no `**Testable:**` lines. Body length is judged separately: most bodies are one to three sentences, and a longer body is noted, not a failure.
expectations.evidence: 6 new criteria from the diff: TKT-014, TKT-015, TKT-016, CLI-010, CLI-011, CLI-012 (check_run's 12/16 include existing headings). Correct headings, unique, no Testable lines. CLI-011 (two paragraphs, 7 sentences) and TKT-016 (3 sentences + example) are longer than typical.

expectations.text: Criteria cover: the OVERDUE marker in `list` output; the `overdue` command's filter; the oldest-due-first order; a ticket exactly at its due time; closed tickets (either excluded, or an open question); and what the user sees when nothing is overdue (output and exit code).
expectations.evidence: Marker: CLI-010 '#<id> [<priority>] <state> OVERDUE <title>' with a 3-line example. Filter: CLI-011 'prints no line for a `closed` ticket or for a ticket that is not yet overdue'. Order: TKT-016 'sorted by due time, earliest first... ID ascending' + example. Exact due: TKT-014 'At its due time exactly, a ticket is not yet overdue.' Closed: TKT-014 'never overdue'. Empty: CLI-011 'With no overdue tickets, or with no log file, it prints nothing and exits with code 0'. Stated as a criterion, not flagged as an assumption.

expectations.text: Every criterion body is behavioral: no function, class, module, or file names (such as TicketService, due_at, cli.py); outcomes are described as what the user sees in the CLI output or exit code.
expectations.evidence: No implementation names in new bodies (impl_words=0; the only .py hit in the diff is the existing AGENTS.md 'Touching tickets.py' column). Outcomes are CLI lines, stdout, exit codes.

expectations.text: The spec respects INV-001 and INV-002: overdue is a derived state computed from the ticket's due time and is not written to the event log; if the spec proposes a new event kind, it flags that as a change to LOG-002 and the invariants needing sign-off.
expectations.evidence: Header: 'The log never records that a ticket became overdue.' TKT-015: 'Becoming overdue appends no event.' Non-goal: 'No new state and no new event kind. TKT-001 and LOG-002 stay as they are.' INV-001/INV-002 not cited by ID.

expectations.text: The spec does not contradict TKT-005 (due time by priority) or TKT-013 (listing order of `list`): it reuses the existing due time and states how OVERDUE interacts with the existing list order rather than redefining it.
expectations.evidence: TKT-014 'its due time, see TKT-005'. Amended CLI-006 keeps 'in ID order, see TKT-013'; CLI-010: 'The lines of all other tickets stay as CLI-006 describes them' with an ID-ordered example. Order not redefined; no explicit 'order stays' sentence.
